text:
olga: hi folks, i'm on my first-week capstone and trying to run repeated generation and embedding calls against the sandbox. after ~10 minutes i start seeing 429s and occasionally 503s. what's the fastest way to understand if it's a quota limit or transient infra?

pri: welcome olga! quick troubleshooting: check response headers (use curl -i). look for X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After on 429s. 503s might be transient; log the response body and timestamps to correlate.

devops: also check X-Quota-Bucket header which tells you whether you're hitting the sandbox pool or a hosted pool. If X-Quota-Bucket mentions "sandbox" then it's quota-related. If headers are missing, paste an example response and we'll take a look.

olga: ah i didn't know about X-Quota-Bucket. example from a 429: 'HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 45
X-Quota-Bucket: sandbox-77'

pri: yup that shows sandbox throttling. two quick fixes: (1) reduce request concurrency and batch more items per call, (2) implement exponential backoff with jitter honoring Retry-After. For embeddings use the batch endpoint to amortize overhead.

devops: operationally, for a short capstone run we can temporarily bump sandbox throughput. open a support ticket in #help or through Console > Support and include: account id, requested tokens/min or requests/min, start/end times, and a short justification. Small requests are usually approved within business hours.

olga: if we need sustained higher throughput beyond a one-off window what's the recommended path?

pri: for sustained workloads we move to a hosted dev seat or a dedicated dev pool. Hosted keys are billed and tied to your org billing; that requires approval from your manager/product owner to enable billing. If you expect long-running heavy jobs, file a request and mention "sustained usage" so we route to sales/partner ops.

devops: another common pattern is a single enqueue-and-drain worker: interns or folks write tasks to a queue (pubsub/sqs) and one worker polls and calls the API at a controlled rate. This prevents many clients from colliding on the same sandbox key.

olga: network note: i'm behind corp vpn and streaming failures earlier. non-streaming calls succeed. any tips?

pri: corp proxies often break websockets/long-lived streams. use the chunked HTTPS endpoint instead of WS while on corp network, or run the client from a machine outside the proxy. Also ensure HTTPS_PROXY is set if your environment requires it.

support-bot: reminder: sandbox keys are shared and limited. Excessive parallel traffic can trigger temporary cooldowns. See onboarding docs: https://console.redwood.dev/docs/onboarding/sandbox-usage

olga: great, thanks. i'll add backoff + batching, queue the capstone jobs to a single worker, and open a support ticket for a short sandbox bump with the details you listed. appreciate the quick help! :smile:
